author: Langston Hughes
title: The Weary Blues
edition: New York: Alfred A. Knopf, 1926. Project Gutenberg English transcription, eBook 74745. HTML verse-line and stanza boundaries retained; indentation and within-line whitespace normalized; page-number furniture omitted; typography and transcription spellings retained. No introduction or digitizer notes included. “Mother to Son” was checked word by word on 2026-11-18 against the printed page, page [107], in the HathiTrust full-view copy of this edition, mdp.39015003918797 (University of Michigan, Google-digitized; https://hdl.handle.net/2027/mdp.39015003918797, the copy the page image itself names), seen as page 114 of the Wikimedia Commons scan “File:The weary blues - 1926.djvu” (whose description names the sibling copy mdp.39015003918763 of the same catalogue record); one transcription error, also in Project Gutenberg’s HTML, was corrected to the print: “I’se been a-climbin’ on” (transcribed “a-cimbin’”). One existing reading (the Grade 7 school night of the poem) changed.

rights.basis: This original English edition was published in 1926, before 1931, and its US term has expired by 2026. Project Gutenberg explicitly identifies this eBook as public domain in the USA. No later introduction, translation, or editorial notes are included.

acquisition.method: Project Gutenberg 74745 HTML from the PG mirror aleph.pglaf.org. Removed the PG header and footer, cover and title-page imprint, copyright leaf, contents, images, page numbers and transcriber matter, and Carl Van Vechten's introduction. Kept the author's dedication and acknowledgment, then every section and poem in printed order: section and poem titles as headings (level 2 and 3), each stanza element one stanza with its verse lines, indentation removed; dedication lines and epigraphs as paragraphs; HTML italics as _underscores_. PG's marked corrections (two title readings) are kept as the transcription prints them. The emendation from the 2026-11-18 check of “Mother to Son” against the print (see edition) is applied to the converted text.
